record.final_answer:
No. That report cannot answer the question — TLS was not measured in it.

What the report actually says (Marrowlog 2.4 performance report, 2026 Q2, published 2026-06-18):
  Result: 180,000 lines/s from one agent on 1 vCPU / 2 GiB, CPU at 85%.
  Method: lines 200 bytes or shorter, output to collector over plain TCP, disk buffer off, batch_lines 500, median of three 30-min runs.
  Not covered: "TLS to the collector, lines longer than 200 bytes, and the disk buffer were not measured. We plan to measure TLS in the Q4 report."

So every number in it is a plain-TCP number. Using it to sign off TLS would be an extrapolation the vendor explicitly declines to make.

Even setting TLS aside, the run isn't comparable to our workload (from /stand/ws/README.md and config/agent.yaml):
  - Line size: their cap is 200 bytes; ours average ~900 bytes (JSON with stack traces).
  - Throughput in bytes: their run moved ~36 MB/s at 85% CPU. Our peak is 50,000 lines/s x ~900 B = ~45 MB/s — 125% of the bytes that saturated their vCPU, even though it's only 28% of their line count.
  - Headroom: 85% CPU leaves ~15%. TLS adds encryption and handshake CPU on exactly the shipping path that was already near saturation, so capacity drops below 45 MB/s, not toward it.

Bottom line for security: the report is not evidence our agents keep up with TLS on. What would be: run our own load test under TLS at 50k lines/s with ~900-byte lines on one vCPU, and watch CPU (CPU saturation, not line rate, is the binding constraint here). Alternatively, wait for the Q4 report — but it still won't cover 900-byte lines or the disk buffer, so a local run is the reliable path.

One thing worth deciding before that test: whether the collector endpoint stays at collector.int.example:6510 with TLS on the same port, or moves to a TLS-specific port — that changes what the test targets.
